name: Partially Involuting Congenital Hemangioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Hemangiomas

criteria.description: Presence of a fully formed vascular tumor at birth
Partial regression of the lesion within the first year of life without complete resolution
Characteristic imaging findings on Doppler ultrasound or MRI showing high-flow vascular channels with partial involution
Negative immunohistochemical staining for GLUT1 differentiating from infantile hemangioma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a congenital vascular tumor with partial involution and characteristic imaging features, plus GLUT1 negativity to exclude infantile hemangioma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathological confirmation may be required in atypical cases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital fully formed vascular tumor present at birth
Partial involution of the hemangioma within the first year of life

common.symptomName: High-flow vascular channels detectable on Doppler ultrasound
searchTerms: fast blood flow in vessels on ultrasound

common.symptomName: Firm, compressible cutaneous mass with overlying telangiectasia
searchTerms: skin growth with visible small blood vessels
red or discolored skin around lesion

common.symptomName: Mild localized edema adjacent to the lesion

searchTerms: reduced blood platelets associated with mass

occasional.symptomName: Pain or tenderness localized to the lesion
Peripheral bruit or thrill over the lesion
searchTerms: bruit or thrill felt on mass

rare.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure secondary to large vascular shunting
searchTerms: heart failure from large blood vessel shunt
heart strain due to vascular tumor

laboratory: Normal or mildly decreased platelet count in some cases
Normal coagulation profile unless Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon develops
imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing high-flow vascular channels
MRI demonstrating well-circumscribed vascular mass with partial involution features
genetic: No known consistent genetic mutations identified
other: Negative GLUT1 immunohistochemical staining differentiates from infantile hemangioma

distinguishingFeatures: Not fully formed at birth, typically appears within weeks after birth
Similar congenital presentation but faster regression

redFlags: Rapid enlargement of lesion with ulceration
references: Dubois J, et al. Congenital hemangiomas: clinical and imaging features. Pediatr Radiol. 2010.
Haggstrom AN, et al. Congenital hemangiomas: clinical and histopathologic features. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2006.
